correctness.rationale: Idempotent maps fix their images. Partition by image cardinality and overlap with a prescribed subset, then inclusion-exclusion counts precisely those outside-image assignments hitting the chosen new target points. This gives every K entry for all n and boundaries; conditional image cardinality alone determines the next rank. Strictly nested injectivity events give unique maximal transient diagonal eigenvalue and a positive rank-two path gives matching asymptotic lower bound. The finite direct-function checker matches all rows n<=6 and all pair products n<=4, including 48 versus 36.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Broad existence and generation theorems concern which maps arise as products, not how many ordered uniform idempotent tuples produce each rank. Even unrestricted random-function distribution cannot simply specialize to idempotent factors, because conditioning every factor to be idempotent changes the joint law. No inspected broader theorem determines these precise probabilities.

originality.rationale: Within actually inspected published material, no statement gives the integer transfer kernel for the ranks of compositions of independent uniform idempotent total maps, its arbitrary-length matrix-power count, or the sharp rank-two survival exponent. Structural factorization, qualitative rank-preservation, unit-regularity and quasi-idempotent generation results are distinct. The elementary occupancy ingredients are known; a differently framed equivalent law remains a genuine residual risk.

value.rationale: The rank kernel is a complete natural finite-state multiplication invariant for arbitrarily long products of independent uniformly sampled idempotents in T_n. It gives exact product-rank distributions, mean synchronization times, a sharp fixed-n exponential synchronization rate, and the first directional product-rank asymmetry, directly relevant to fundamental semigroup factorization and synchronizing transformation systems; it is not just an isolated small census.
